description:
AstroSprout — Growing Smarter, From Space!

We are joining the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge to build data-driven solutions for climate-resilient agriculture. We combine NASA climate data, satellite imagery, soil moisture, and agricultural data to assess crop suitability and water stress.
summary:
AstroSprout is an agricultural decision-support platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into localized crop suitability insights for Egypt. The project addresses the challenges of climate variability, water scarcity, and regional differences in agricultural conditions by providing data-driven support for smarter crop selection and seasonal planning.

We assembled a historical environmental dataset covering 25 Egyptian governorates and 141 geographic sampling points from 2016 to 2025, using NASA POWER meteorological and soil-wetness variables alongside MODIS MOD13Q1 vegetation indices (NDVI and EVI). AstroSprout combines a regional data-processing workflow with an implemented rule-based crop ranking and suitability scoring prototype. We are developing a machine-learning forecasting layer, benchmarking OLS, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting using MAE, with the goal of integrating environmental predictions into future multi-season and five-year agricultural planning.

By making environmental data more accessible and crop recommendations more transparent, AstroSprout aims to support climate-aware agriculture and more responsible water and soil resource management.
details:
AstroSprout is an agricultural decision-support platform designed to help address climate variability, water scarcity, and changing environmental conditions across Egypt.

The platform combines NASA POWER meteorological and soil-wetness data with MODIS MOD13Q1 vegetation indices (NDVI and EVI) to analyze environmental conditions across 25 Egyptian governorates and 141 geographic sampling points, using historical data from 2016 to 2025.

AstroSprout follows a hybrid architecture. Its implemented rule-based crop suitability engine evaluates crop-specific conditions, seasonal requirements, and environmental constraints to rank potential crops and generate suitability scores. A machine-learning forecasting layer is under development, with OLS, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting selected as candidate algorithms. The models are intended to predict environmental variables, with Mean Absolute Error (MAE) used for evaluation before future integration into crop suitability and multi-season planning.

The platform aims to make complex Earth observation data more accessible and useful for agricultural decision-making. Its intended impact includes supporting climate-aware crop selection, promoting responsible water and soil resource management, and enabling more localized agricultural planning.

The project combines geospatial data processing, environmental analysis, machine learning, and interactive web development. Its creative approach is to connect historical NASA environmental observations with explainable crop-ranking logic in one regional agricultural decision-support workflow.

Key factors considered include geographic variation, seasonal crop requirements, temperature extremes, precipitation, humidity, soil moisture, vegetation health, and the limitations of gridded environmental data. Future development aims to extend this approach toward predictive, multi-season agricultural planning.
